entryWatch.setup: MDT day-2 continuation after the 9/1 beat-and-raise - the name the 9/1 file flagged as worth this open's attention if it built a shelf. It built it. The 9/1 reaction bar opened 94.00, ran 95.41, flushed to 90.80 and closed 92.04 on 18.8M shares against roughly 6.5M typical - a faded gap that nonetheless HELD 1.53% above the 90.65 pre-print close, which is the exact line SAIC and NTNX failed. The afternoon based 92.24-92.96 for four hours. Today opened 91.47, below yesterday's close and below that base, held above the 90.80 reaction low, and reversed to a 93.39 high. SPECIFIED at 09:45 at a 93.07 limit for 4 shares, CLEAN, no checklist item marked fail, struck AT THE OFFER rather than under the bid as the direct correction to yesterday's DG failure.
entryWatch.trigger: LIVE SPECIFICATION, expiring 15:30 ET today. MDT 92.99 bid / 93.07 ask at 2026-09-02T13:45:07.021554173Z, last 93.04, +1.09% against a 92.04 settled close, on a 0.08 spread that is 0.086% of mark. Limit 93.07, target 111.68, stop 85.62, time stop the 9/9 close. FOUR NAMED INVALIDATIONS, any one of which kills the spec by appending: a trade below 91.47 (today's opening low, the low the reversal is built on); a trade below 90.80 (the 9/1 reaction-bar low, below which the gap is round-tripping and the name has become SAIC); any close below 90.65 (the 8/31 pre-print close, the full round-trip); or MDT closing red on a day XLV closes green (relative-strength failure). THE COUNTERWEIGHT THE HOURLIES MUST KEEP CHECKING: healthcare is today's leading sector with XLV +1.57%, BSX +1.87%, ABT +1.49%, BDX +1.31% and ZBH +1.14% against SPY +0.13%, so MDT at +1.09% is LAGGING four of five peers and part of today's move is sector beta rather than MDT alpha. What is MDT's own is the intraday shape - it opened at -0.62% while the sector opened bid, then reversed through the prior close. An hourly should re-read that relationship, not just the level.
entryWatch.why: The primary case is the day-2 structure off a beat AND raise, not the cohort. That ordering is deliberate: yesterday's DG entry rested on a cohort-laggard framing that inverted by 14:22 while the spec sat unfilled, so the sympathy-laggard reading is available here but is written down as a secondary tailwind rather than the load-bearing claim. Also recorded before the outcome: eight price-target raises landed in one pre-market (Mizuho 100-115, Leerink 104-111, Evercore 105-106, Wells Fargo 102-104, Baird 91-100, Truist 86-99, Stifel 80-95, Jefferies 88-95) with a mean target of 101.74 - which sits BELOW the mechanical +20% take-profit at 111.68. This trade most likely closes on the time stop rather than the target, and it says so at entry rather than discovering it at the retro.

The spec died VALID rather than wrong - none of its three invalidations fired - and it still did not fill, because it was struck 0.38% under the bid of a name that rose on every bar. Today's MDT entry is struck AT the offer for that reason, and this row is what that decision is answering.

entryWatch.why: Recorded as the runner-up rather than dropped, because a mandated entry that does not name what it beat is not gradeable. If MDT fails and OLLI runs, this row is the evidence for whether the reaction-bar refusal was the right call or a reflex.

entryWatch.trigger: STILL REFUSED, AND STILL BREAKING DOWN. SAIC is 123.11 bid / 124.39 ask at 2026-09-02T13:41:55.491665676Z, last 123.50, -2.90% against a 126.78 settled close, on a 1.03% spread. entryWatch.why: This is the row MDT is graded against. Same shape at the start - a large beat, a gap, a fade - and opposite resolutions: SAIC lost its pre-print close on day 2 and MDT held 1.53% above it. The rulebook has no rule that says 'a big beat is a buy'; it has a rule about what the tape does with the gap, and these two names are the worked example of why.
